newsitem.title: UK: London freight - BFI down 3, heavy grain rates dip.
newsitem.headline: London freight - BFI down 3, heavy grain rates dip.

text.p: The Baltic Freight Index (BFI) dipped three points to 1,460 points on Tuesday but the Baltic Handy Index posted a gain of 13 point to 1,079.
Brokers said that the BFI dropped again as U.S. Gulf/Japan grain business rates continued to decline, although this situation wasn't expected to last for more than a week a two.
Over coming weeks, there was likely to be upward pressure for rates as charterers looked to ship grain out of the U.S. and South America, they added.

Fresh grain fixing was reported on the U.S. Gulf/Japan route, with both Choyang and Hanjin fixing 54,000 tonnes heavy grain around mid March at $25.25, slightly down on similar business recently at $25.50.

At the close, the BIFFEX futures were 10 points up to five points down. Most active March closed five points firmer at 1,540 after 29 lots traded, while April ended 10 points higher at 1,550. Volume totalled 46 lots.
Brokers said that the gains on March and April Biffex futures probably reflected expectations of an increase in major grain shipments during that period.

On timecharters, a number of panamxes were fixed for delivery Japan early March trip Pacific r/v. However, rates varied as the Western Trader was taken for $12,100 daily, while the rate for the Kostrena was in the low $11,000s daily.
In the mineral sector, I.L.P. fixed 100,000 tonnes coal Hampton Roads/Taranto Feb 25-Mar 4 at $6.40.
Ore trade saw Baosteel fix 150,000 tonnes W.Australia/China Feb 15-Mar 30 at $4.85.
Capesize business rates looked like they are stabilising as more forward cargoes become available, brokers said.
But with plenty of prompt tonnage available, any recovery could be a while yet, they added.
